findings.value: REDEMPTION (gaal/geullah/padah) - recovered after an extraction gap (gaal/geullah were never registered as terms; the kinsman-redeemer vocabulary, 18 tokens in the text, was invisible until re-coded from verse_span_index). It centres on the KINSMAN-REDEEMER (go'el): a near relative may BUY BACK what poverty forced away - land, a house, and above all a PERSON sold into slavery (25:49 - uncle, cousin, or clan-relative may redeem him, or he redeems himself if he prospers) - RESTORING the lost one to freedom and family. Redemption also applies to what is dedicated to the LORD (ch27: redeem by valuation + a fifth), EXCEPT the cherem (devoted/banned thing) and the tithe, which are IRREDEEMABLE (27:28,33). Set beside atonement, the two complete each other: ATONEMENT (kaphar 17:11) covers the guilty before God by a LIFE given; REDEMPTION (gaal) buys the lost back into belonging by a PRICE paid by a kinsman. The nephesh is both atoned-for (life-for-life) and redeemable (bought back) - the seed of the biblical go'el/Redeemer theme (Ruth; Job 19:25; Isaiah 'the LORD your Redeemer').
